# vite-plugin-tiny-state

> Vite plugin (npm: `@jswork/vite-plugin-tiny-state`) for zero-config auto-discovery and registration of `@jswork/react-tiny-state` store modules.

The plugin automates store module discovery in Vite projects:
1. Dynamically generates a virtual module `virtual:tiny-state` that executes `nx.$registerStores(import.meta.glob('/src/stores/**/*.ts', { eager: true, import: 'default' }))`.
2. Automatically injects `import 'virtual:tiny-state';` into the application entry point (`src/main.tsx`) at compile time.
3. Developers can create store modules under `src/stores/` without writing any manual `import` or registration code in the app.

## Quick Start

### 1. Configure Vite (`vite.config.ts`)

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import vitePluginTinyState from '@jswork/vite-plugin-tiny-state';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    vitePluginTinyState(), // Zero configuration auto-registration
  ],
});
```

### 2. Define Stores (`src/stores/*.ts` or `src/stores/**/*.ts`)

Store files export a store descriptor wrapped with `nx.$defineStore`:

```ts
// src/stores/counter.ts -> module name: counter
import nx from '@jswork/next';

export default nx.$defineStore({
  state: { count: 0 },
  getters: {
    double: (state) => state.count * 2,
  },
  actions: {
    increment: (state) => nx.$set('counter.count', state.count + 1),
    decrement: (state) => nx.$set('counter.count', state.count - 1),
    reset: () => nx.$set('counter.count', 0),
  },
});
```

#### Nested Subdirectories

Nested directories automatically convert to camelCase module names:
- `src/stores/member/profile.ts` -> Module name: `memberProfile`
- `src/stores/member/orders.ts` -> Module name: `memberOrders`
- `src/stores/member/index.ts` -> Module name: `member` (strips `/index`)

```ts
// src/stores/member/profile.ts -> module name: memberProfile
import nx from '@jswork/next';

export default nx.$defineStore({
  state: {
    nickname: 'Alice',
    vipLevel: 1,
  },
  actions: {
    setNickname: (_state, _getters, name: string) => nx.$set('memberProfile.nickname', name),
  },
});
```

### 3. Consume in React Components

No store imports needed inside components. Directly use `nx` global methods:

```tsx
import nx from '@jswork/next';

export default function CounterView() {
  // Read reactive state
  const count = nx.$use('counter.count');
  const double = nx.$use('counter.double');
  const nickname = nx.$use('memberProfile.nickname');

  return (
    <div>
      <p>User: {nickname}</p>
      <p>Count: {count} (Double: {double})</p>
      <button onClick={() => nx.$call('counter.increment')}>+1</button>
      <button onClick={() => nx.$set('memberProfile.nickname', 'Bob')}>Change Name</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Options

```ts
interface TinyStatePluginOptions {
  /**
   * Glob pattern to scan store modules.
   * Supports single or nested subdirectories.
   * @default '/src/stores/**\/*.ts'
   */
  pattern?: string;

  /**
   * Automatically inject `import 'virtual:tiny-state';` into entry file.
   * Set to `false` if you prefer importing `virtual:tiny-state` manually.
   * @default true
   */
  autoInject?: boolean;

  /**
   * Target entry file path substring to inject virtual module.
   * @default 'src/main.tsx'
   */
  entry?: string;
}
```

## TypeScript Configuration

If TypeScript complains about `virtual:tiny-state`, add the following to `src/vite-env.d.ts`:

```ts
declare module 'virtual:tiny-state' {
  export const stores: Record<string, any>;
  export default stores;
}
```
